---
title: "The nine-species benchmark, version by version"
subtitle: "Every public copy of the benchmark, compared spectrum by spectrum"
description: "The nine-species de novo sequencing benchmark exists in at least eleven public versions. Every spectrum followed from one to the next: splits, labels, precursors, peaks, and how much of one version's test set another version trained on. Every number links to the code that computes it."
---

"Evaluated on nine-species" names at least eleven different sets of spectra.
This page puts every public copy of the benchmark on one key, *(species, raw
file, scan)*, and follows each spectrum from one version to the next: whether
it stays, which split it lands in, whether its label changes, and whether the
spectrum itself does. It was computed on 2026-10-20 from the files as
published that day.

**Every number is a link.** It leads to an entry in
[Reproducing every number](#reproducing-every-number) at the end of the page,
which names the public files it reads, the scripts that produce its input, and
the code that counts it. The whole analysis reruns from those files with one
script, [`run_all.sh`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/run_all.sh).
The catalog's own record of the versions is the
[nine-species benchmark's page](../datasets/nine-species-benchmark.html).

**Naming.** Papers call DeepNovo's 2017 release "9-species-V1" and the
re-curated benchmark "9-species-V2", usually without saying which file. Here
**v1** is the 2017 release and **v2 main** and **v2 balanced** are the two
variants [Wen & Noble](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-04068-4) published in
[10.5281/zenodo.13685813](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13685813). The three
dated folders of [MSV000090982](https://massive.ucsd.edu/ProteoSAFe/dataset.jsp?accession=MSV000090982)
are earlier **builds of v2**, and none of them is v2 main.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Four things to know before quoting a nine-species number.**

1. **MSV000090982 is not v2 main.** It holds three builds, from 2022, 2023 and
   2024, and even the 2024 build is {{n:r2024_main_diff}} spectra away from v2
   main.
2. **The InstaNovo split, which NovoBench trains on, overlaps the newer test
   sets.** {{n:leak_pb_pct}} of ProteoBench's spectra, {{n:leak_dion_pct}} of
   dIon's test set and {{n:leak_dnb_pct}} of denovo_benchmarks' nine-species
   sets are scans from its training split.
3. **One v2 spectrum in six has a precursor on an isotope peak**
   ({{n:iso_main_pct}} of v2 main). A model that enforces the precursor mass with
   no isotope allowance cannot get those right; on v1 and on the InstaNovo split
   that never happens.
4. **v1 writes every leucine as I** ({{n:v1_labels_with_l}} of its labels contain an L).
   Fold I and L before comparing labels across versions.
:::

The same Zenodo record [10.5281/zenodo.13685813](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13685813)
also holds [`nine-species-intermediate.zip`](https://zenodo.org/records/13685813/files/nine-species-intermediate.zip),
the Tide and Percolator output ({{n:perc_target_psms}} target PSMs over
{{n:perc_target_scans}} scans), and [`nine-species-data.zip`](https://zenodo.org/records/13685813/files/nine-species-data.zip),
the converted MGFs before any search ({{n:converted}} MS2 spectra from
{{n:raw_files_converted}} raw files).

A **backbone** is the bare sequence with I and L folded together, the grain at
which two labels can be the same peptide.

## How the spectra flow between versions

Every spectrum that any version holds, counted once per column. The first
column says where it started: in which split of the InstaNovo split (which is
also NovoBench's), elsewhere in v1, or not in v1 at all. The second says which
revised version holds it, and the third where it sits inside v2 main. Each band
keeps the colour of its starting point, so the training split can be followed
into v2 balanced, which is ProteoBench.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
d3s = require("d3-sankey@0.12.3")
sankey_chart = {
  const W = Math.min(width, 1000), H = 560, M = {top: 34, right: 230, bottom: 8, left: 245}
  const origin_colour = new Map([["InstaNovo train", "#dc2626"], ["InstaNovo valid", "#f97316"],
    ["InstaNovo test", "#eab308"], ["v1, outside the InstaNovo split", "#64748b"], ["not in v1", "#2563eb"]])
  const s1 = d3.rollups(ns.sankey, v => d3.sum(v, d => d.n), d => d.c1, d => d.c2)
    .flatMap(([a, bs]) => bs.map(([b, n]) => ({source: a, target: b, value: n, origin: a})))
  const s2 = d3.rollups(ns.sankey.filter(d => d.c3), v => d3.sum(v, d => d.n), d => d.c2, d => d.c3, d => d.c1)
    .flatMap(([a, cs]) => cs.flatMap(([c, os]) => os.map(([o, n]) => ({source: a, target: c, value: n, origin: o}))))
  const names = [...new Set([...s1, ...s2].flatMap(l => [l.source, l.target]))]
  // sankeyLeft keeps a node in its own column: the default justifies every node with no
  // outgoing band to the last column, which put "a MassIVE build of v2 only" under "Inside v2 main".
  const graph = d3s.sankey().nodeId(d => d.name).nodeAlign(d3s.sankeyLeft).nodeWidth(14).nodePadding(16)
    .nodeSort((a, b) => b.value - a.value)
    .extent([[M.left, M.top], [W - M.right, H - M.bottom]])({
      nodes: names.map(name => ({name})), links: [...s1, ...s2].map(d => ({...d}))})
  const svg = d3.create("svg").attr("viewBox", [0, 0, W, H])
    .attr("style", "max-width:100%; height:auto; font:11px sans-serif;")
  svg.append("g").attr("fill", "none").selectAll("path").data(graph.links).join("path")
    .attr("d", d3s.sankeyLinkHorizontal()).attr("stroke", d => origin_colour.get(d.origin))
    .attr("stroke-opacity", 0.45).attr("stroke-width", d => Math.max(1, d.width))
    .append("title").text(d => `${d.origin}: ${d.source.name} → ${d.target.name}\n${d3.format(",")(d.value)} spectra`)
  svg.append("g").selectAll("rect").data(graph.nodes).join("rect")
    .attr("x", d => d.x0).attr("y", d => d.y0).attr("width", d => d.x1 - d.x0)
    .attr("height", d => Math.max(1, d.y1 - d.y0))
    .attr("fill", d => origin_colour.get(d.name) ?? "#334155")
    .append("title").text(d => `${d.name}\n${d3.format(",")(d.value)} spectra`)
  svg.append("g").selectAll("text").data(graph.nodes).join("text")
    .attr("x", d => d.depth === 0 ? d.x0 - 6 : d.x1 + 6).attr("y", d => (d.y0 + d.y1) / 2)
    .attr("dy", "0.35em").attr("text-anchor", d => d.depth === 0 ? "end" : "start")
    // A white halo, because the middle column's labels sit over the bands leaving it.
    .attr("paint-order", "stroke").attr("stroke", "white").attr("stroke-width", 3)
    .text(d => `${d.name} · ${d3.format(",")(d.value)}`)
  const cols = ["Where it started", "Which revised version holds it", "Inside v2 main"]
  const xs = [...new Set(graph.nodes.map(d => d.x0))].sort((a, b) => a - b)
  svg.append("g").selectAll("text").data(xs).join("text")
    .attr("x", (x, i) => i === 0 ? x + 14 : x).attr("y", 14).attr("font-weight", "bold")
    .attr("text-anchor", (x, i) => i === 0 ? "end" : "start").text((x, i) => cols[i])
  return svg.node()
}
```

Read from left to right: of the InstaNovo split's {{n:instanovo_train}} training
spectra, almost half are in v2 main, and some of those land in v2 balanced and
in dIon. Most of the rest went nowhere in v2 (the next section says why), and
some only into denovo_benchmarks. The blue band, the spectra v1 never had, is
most of v2. Hover a band for its count.

## Where v1's spectra went

{{n:fate_kept_pct}} of v1's {{n:v1_psms}} labelled spectra are in v2 main. Each
of the others was dropped at a step of the revised pipeline that can be named,
by asking the revised search itself about that scan.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
fate_order = ["kept in v2 main", "raw file not in the revised search", "no target PSM for the scan",
              "failed 1% FDR, same peptide", "failed 1% FDR, other peptide",
              "passed, but the MGF gives no precursor charge",
              "passed, but its peptide was drawn for another species"]
// The CSV's columns are numbered steps of the pipeline ("3a failed ..."); the number names the fate.
// Parenthesised: in OJS `name = {...}` is a block, not an object literal.
fate_of = ({"0": 0, "1": 1, "2": 2, "3a": 3, "3b": 4, "4a": 5, "4c": 6})
fate_rows = ns.fate_by_species.flatMap(r => Object.entries(r)
  .filter(([k]) => k !== "species")
  .map(([k, v]) => ({species: r.species, fate: fate_order[fate_of[k.split(" ")[0]]], n: v})))
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 330, marginLeft: 110, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Share of v1's spectra in that species", percent: true, labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: d3.groupSort(fate_rows, g => -d3.sum(g.filter(d => d.fate === fate_order[0]), d => d.n) / d3.sum(g, d => d.n), d => d.species)},
  color: {domain: fate_order, range: ["#16a34a", "#94a3b8", "#cbd5e1", "#fbbf24", "#d97706", "#7c3aed", "#2563eb"],
          legend: true, columns: 2},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(fate_rows, Plot.stackX({offset: "normalize", order: fate_order,
      x: "n", y: "species", fill: "fate", tip: {format: {x: false}, channels: {Spectra: "n"}}})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

| fate | spectra |
|---|---:|
| kept in v2 main | {{n:fate_kept}} |
| raw file not in the revised search (honeybee `BM-2`) | {{n:fate_raw_missing}} |
| the revised search reported no target PSM for the scan | {{n:fate_no_psm}} |
| best PSM failed the 1% FDR, same peptide as v1 | {{n:fate_fdr_same}} |
| best PSM failed the 1% FDR, another peptide | {{n:fate_fdr_other}} |
| passed, but the converted MGF gives no precursor charge | {{n:fate_nocharge}} |
| passed, but its peptide was found in several species and drawn for another | {{n:fate_shared}} |

Every scan the revised search reported nothing for was converted and searched
({{n:nopsm_with_charge}} with a precursor charge, {{n:nopsm_without_charge}}
without); its best match was simply a decoy, or nothing at all. Of the
spectra kept, {{n:kept_same}} keep their backbone and modifications,
{{n:kept_mods}} keep the backbone with different modifications, and
{{n:kept_diff}} are relabelled as another peptide. Compared without folding I
and L, {{n:orig_label_il_only}} of them would look like label changes.

## From raw files to v2 main, and a filter the paper does not mention

The converted MGFs in [`nine-species-data.zip`](https://zenodo.org/records/13685813/files/nine-species-data.zip)
let the whole pipeline be replayed in counts.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
funnel = {
  const all = ns.converted.find(d => d.species === "ALL")
  return [
    {step: "MS2 spectra converted", n: all["converted MS2"]},
    {step: "best Percolator match is a target", n: all["target PSM"]},
    {step: "that PSM has q < 0.01", n: all["q<0.01"]},
    {step: "and the MGF gives a charge", n: all["q<0.01"] - all["q<0.01, no charge"]},
    {step: "v2 main", n: ns.build_counts.find(d => d.build === "zenodo_main" && d.species === "ALL").n}
  ]
}
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 230, marginLeft: 230, marginRight: 80, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Spectra (millions)", transform: d => d / 1e6, labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: funnel.map(d => d.step)},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(funnel, {x: "n", y: "step", fill: "#2563eb"}),
    Plot.text(funnel, {x: "n", y: "step", text: d => d3.format(",")(d.n), dx: 6, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 11}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

**Not one spectrum in v2 main lacks a precursor charge** ({{n:nocharge_in_main}}),
although {{n:nocharge_total}} of the converted spectra do and the search ran on
all of them: {{n:nocharge_human_pct}} of the human spectra,
{{n:nocharge_cendo_pct}} of *C. endoloripes*' and {{n:nocharge_bsub_pct}} of
*B. subtilis*'. Percolator accepted {{n:nocharge_passing}} of them and every one
was dropped. [Wen & Noble](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-024-04068-4) do not
describe this step. They report dropping "13 MGF files with fewer than 100
accepted PSMs", and those are {{n:bsub_chargeless_files}} *B. subtilis* files in
which no spectrum has a charge at all ({{n:bsub_file_psm_min}} to
{{n:bsub_file_psm_max}} accepted PSMs each, and a DIA run with 1): they fall
under 100 only once the charge-less ones are gone. {{n:mouse_dropped_files}}
mouse files with almost nothing accepted leave {{n:raw_files_main}} raw files in
v2 main. Subtracting the charge-less spectra and those mouse files gives
{{n:after_filters}}, the paper's 2,898,611 within 3, and the shared-peptide draw
then removes {{n:shared_draw_removed}} more. denovo_benchmarks applies the same
charge filter when it builds a dataset.

## What changed in the spectra that stayed

v1 was exported by PEAKS in 2017 and v2 by ThermoRawFileParser in 2022, and the
two disagree about the spectrum itself.

**The precursor m/z.** Among the {{n:v1_2022_shared}} spectra v1 shares with the
2022 build, {{n:v1_2022_plus1}} have a neutral precursor mass 1 Da heavier in the
revised version and {{n:v1_2022_plus2}} 2 Da heavier. Every precursor in v1 sits
on its label's monoisotopic peak ({{n:iso_v1}} on an isotope peak);
ThermoRawFileParser writes the m/z the instrument selected, which is often an
isotope peak. The revised search "allowed for 1 isotope error in the selection
of candidate peptides" (Wen & Noble, Methods), and the released MGFs keep the
instrument's m/z.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Column in the data -> label on the page.
iso_versions = new Map([["MassIVE r2022", "v2, MassIVE 2022"], ["MassIVE r2023", "v2, MassIVE 2023"],
                        ["MassIVE r2024", "v2, MassIVE 2024"], ["Zenodo main", "v2 main"],
                        ["Zenodo balanced = ProteoBench", "v2 balanced = ProteoBench"], ["dIon", "dIon"]])
iso_rows = ns.isotope_by_species.flatMap(r => [...iso_versions].map(([col, label]) => ({species: r.species, version: label, pct: r[col]})))
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 420, marginLeft: 110, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Spectra whose precursor is the label's M+1 peak (%)", domain: [0, 32], labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: d3.groupSort(iso_rows, g => -d3.mean(g, d => d.pct), d => d.species)},
  color: {domain: [...iso_versions.values()], scheme: "tableau10", legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.ruleY(d3.groups(iso_rows, d => d.species).map(([s]) => s), {stroke: "#e2e8f0"}),
    // One mark per version, each nudged vertically: the builds sit within a
    // point of each other and drew on top of one another. dy is a constant in
    // Plot, not a channel, which is why this is six marks and not one.
    ...[...iso_versions.values()].map((v, i) =>
      Plot.dot(iso_rows.filter(d => d.version === v), {x: "pct", y: "species", fill: "version", r: 4,
               dy: (i - 2.5) * 6, stroke: "white", strokeWidth: 0.5, tip: true})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

Over v2 main it is {{n:iso_main}} spectra, {{n:iso_main_pct}}, from
{{n:iso_vmungo_pct}} of *V. mungo* to {{n:iso_yeast_pct}} of yeast; in the
builds {{n:iso_2022_pct}} (2022), {{n:iso_2023_pct}} (2023) and
{{n:iso_2024_pct}} (2024); in v2 balanced and ProteoBench {{n:iso_balanced_pct}};
in dIon {{n:iso_dion_pct}}. The InstaNovo split has {{n:iso_instanovo}}. These
are isotope picks and not missed deamidations, which sit 0.019 Da away: the
error assuming a carbon-13 offset has a median of {{n:iso_c13_median_ppm}}
against {{n:iso_deam_median_ppm}} assuming deamidation, and {{n:iso_no_nq}} of
the offset spectra have no N or Q to deamidate. Casanovo's default allows an
offset of 0 or 1; check what a given model does before comparing its numbers
across the two.

**The peaks.** v1's peak lists are sparser (median {{n:peaks_v1_median}} peaks
against {{n:peaks_v2_median}}) and reach fragment m/z values no fragment of the
precursor can have (up to {{n:frag_v1_max}}, against {{n:frag_v2_max}}). For
mouse, where both sides could be downloaded whole, {{n:mouse_peak_spectra}}
spectra were compared peak by peak: a median {{n:mouse_peaks_matched_pct}} of
v1's peaks are in the revised peak list within 10 ppm, carrying
{{n:mouse_intensity_matched_pct}} of its intensity, and v1's intensities are
about {{n:mouse_intensity_ratio}} times the revised ones. v1 is the same scan
after PEAKS's own processing.

**Everything else** barely moves: {{n:v1_2022_charge_changed}} shared spectra
change charge, the revised builds hold no charge-1 spectra (v1 has
{{n:v1_charge1_pct}}) and no peptide shorter than 6 or longer than 50 residues.

**The modification vocabulary.** v1 and the 2022 build carry oxidation, N and Q
deamidation and carbamidomethylation. From 2023 on, four N-terminal
modifications appear: acetylation (+42.01), carbamylation (+43.01), ammonia loss
(-17.03) and carbamylation with ammonia loss (+25.98), on {{n:nterm_main_pct}}
of v2 main's spectra. A model trained on v1 or on the InstaNovo split has never
seen one.

## Between the builds of v2

| | out | in | label changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| MassIVE 2022 → 2023 | {{n:r2022_r2023_out}} | {{n:r2022_r2023_in}} | {{n:r2022_r2023_relabelled}} |
| MassIVE 2023 → 2024 | {{n:r2023_r2024_out}} | {{n:r2023_r2024_in}} | {{n:r2023_r2024_relabelled}} |
| MassIVE 2024 → v2 main | {{n:r2024_main_out}} | {{n:r2024_main_in}} | 0 |

**2022 to 2023 is a re-search.** {{n:swing_22_23_out_same_pct}} of the spectra
leaving, and {{n:swing_22_23_in_same_pct}} of those arriving, have a peptide the
other build keeps in the same species: different scans of the same peptide
passed the FDR. Of the relabelled spectra, {{n:relabel_deamidation}} gain, lose
or move an N or Q deamidation, {{n:relabel_nterm}} gain an N-terminal
modification, {{n:relabel_same_set}} move an I/L or a modification, and
{{n:relabel_peptide}} change peptide.

**After 2023 every change is the shared-peptide draw.** Wen & Noble give each
peptide found in more than one species to one species at random and drop its
spectra from the others. Re-running that draw moves whole peptides between
species files: {{n:swing_23_24_shared}} of the {{n:r2023_r2024_out}} spectra
leaving between 2023 and 2024, and {{n:swing_main_shared}} of the
{{n:r2024_main_in}} arriving between 2024 and v2 main, carry a peptide found in
more than one species. Backbones present in more than one species file:
{{n:multi_species_r2022}} in 2022, {{n:multi_species_r2023}} in 2023,
{{n:multi_species_r2024}} in 2024, and {{n:multi_species_zenodo_main}} in v2 main.
The benchmark repository cannot regenerate any of them exactly: its seed is
fixed, but the species and file order it draws over come from the filesystem.

## denovo_benchmarks' nine species

The living benchmark's datasets file calls its nine-species sets "De novo
nine-species benchmark (MSV000090982)". They are not. Its own deposit,
[MSV000096182](https://massive.ucsd.edu/ProteoSAFe/dataset.jsp?accession=MSV000096182),
holds {{n:dnb_raw_files}} raw files relabelled by its own search:
{{n:dnb_labels}} labels, keyed as `<raw file>_<chunk>:<index>` into MGF chunks of
at most 20,000 charged spectra.

- **A different subset of files.** Mouse takes all {{n:dnb_mouse_files}} raw
  files, including the ones v2 main drops; *B. subtilis* takes
  {{n:dnb_bsub_files}} of {{n:dnb_bsub_converted}} and yeast
  {{n:dnb_yeast_files}} of {{n:dnb_yeast_converted}}; and honeybee includes
  `BM-2`, the file the revised search never had.
- **Different labels.** Of the {{n:dnb_in_main}} spectra it shares with v2 main,
  {{n:dnb_same_label_pct}} carry the same label; {{n:dnb_not_in_main}} are not
  in v2 main at all. {{n:dnb_rare_mods}} labels carry a modification the revised
  search did not allow: N-terminal, D, E and H carbamidomethylation, sodium on D
  and E, lysine and arginine methylation, and +12 and +26 N-terminal adducts.
- **A deamidation where the others see an isotope peak.** On
  {{n:dnb_iso_spectra}} spectra that v2 main labels at the M+1 peak,
  denovo_benchmarks writes the same backbone with one more deamidation in
  {{n:dnb_iso_deamidation}} cases. The carbon-13 reading fits better for
  {{n:dnb_c13_better}} of them (median error {{n:dnb_c13_ppm}} against
  {{n:dnb_deam_ppm}}), so these labels most likely carry a deamidation that is
  not there.
- **A deposit that does not match its labels in two files.**
  {{n:dnb_unresolved}} labels point past the end of their MGF chunk (`BC-2_1`
  holds {{n:dnb_bc2_1_spectra}} spectra and is cited up to index
  {{n:dnb_bc2_1_max_index}}), so those chunks are not the files the labels were
  made from.

## Splits, and what a model has already seen

**v1's folds are disjoint on the modified peptide, not on the backbone.** No
validation or test label of a fold is a training label of that fold, but
{{n:fold_backbone_min}} to {{n:fold_backbone_max}} of every fold's validation
and test spectra carry a backbone it trains on, in another modification state.
Across species, the held-out species' spectra whose backbone the fold trained on
run from {{n:heldout_min_pct}} (*M. mazei*) to {{n:heldout_max_pct}}
(*V. mungo*). v2 was built to remove that, and did: {{n:multi_species_zenodo_main}}
backbones of v2 main are in two species.

**The InstaNovo split is v1's yeast fold**, the same training spectra NovoBench
retrains on, in v1's own order: row by row, {{n:instanovo_row_aligned}} of its
{{n:instanovo_all}} records have the precursor and peak count of the v1 record
in the same position of the yeast-excluded fold's train and valid files, and,
for its test set, of v1's whole yeast file. **Training
on it and testing on another version outside yeast tests partly on training
data**, because the spectra are the same physical scans, re-labelled.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
leak_label = new Map([["InstaNovo test (original yeast file)", "InstaNovo test (v1 yeast)"],
                      ["Zenodo main, all species", "v2 main, all species"], ["Zenodo main, yeast only", "v2 main, yeast only"],
                      ["Zenodo balanced = ProteoBench", "v2 balanced = ProteoBench"], ["dIon test", "dIon test"],
                      ["dIon validation", "dIon validation"], ["denovo_benchmarks selection", "denovo_benchmarks"]])
leak_rows = ns.leak.filter(d => leak_label.has(d["evaluate on"])).flatMap(d => [
  {set: leak_label.get(d["evaluate on"]), what: "its backbone is in the training split", pct: d["peptide seen %"]},
  {set: leak_label.get(d["evaluate on"]), what: "the same scan is in the training split", pct: d["same spectrum %"]}])
Plot.plot({
  width: Math.min(width, 1000), height: 300, marginLeft: 220, marginRight: 30, marginBottom: 40,
  x: {label: "Share of the evaluation spectra (%)", domain: [0, 80], labelOffset: 34},
  y: {label: null, domain: [...new Set(leak_rows.map(d => d.set))]},
  color: {domain: ["its backbone is in the training split", "the same scan is in the training split"],
          range: ["#cbd5e1", "#dc2626"], legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("its")), {x: "pct", y: "set", fill: "what"}),
    Plot.barX(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("the same")), {x: "pct", y: "set", fill: "what", insetTop: 5, insetBottom: 5}),
    Plot.text(leak_rows.filter(d => d.what.startsWith("its")), {x: "pct", y: "set", text: d => `${d.pct.toFixed(1)}%`, dx: 5, textAnchor: "start", fontSize: 10}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

ProteoBench's yeast and *B. subtilis* spectra are untouched, but
{{n:leak_pb_mouse_pct}} of its mouse spectra and {{n:leak_pb_human_pct}} of its
human ones are scans a NovoBench-style model was trained on. A number such a
model scores on ProteoBench, on v2 main beyond the yeast file
({{n:leak_main_pct}} training scans, {{n:leak_main_pct_backbone}} known
backbones), on dIon or on denovo_benchmarks is partly a training score.

## What to write when reporting a number

- **Name the build, not the accession.** "9-species-V2" is three builds under
  one MassIVE accession plus v2 main and v2 balanced on Zenodo; InstaNovo's
  `ninespecies_updated` is the 2023 build; denovo_benchmarks is a selection of
  its own.
- **Do not train on the InstaNovo or NovoBench split and test on a newer
  version outside yeast.** Up to {{n:leak_dnb_pct}} of the test spectra are
  training scans, and about {{n:leak_dnb_pct_backbone}} carry a backbone the
  model trained on.
- **Allow a one-dalton precursor offset**, or score the v2 spectra whose
  precursor is an isotope peak separately.
- **Fold I and L before comparing labels across versions.**

## Reproducing this page

Everything above was computed from the public files the versions table links,
by the scripts in
[`analysis/nine_species/`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/tree/main/analysis/nine_species).
To rerun it:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing
mkdir -p ~/data/ninespecies
cp -r awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/analysis/nine_species ~/data/ninespecies/scripts
sh ~/data/ninespecies/scripts/run_all.sh                       # about 110 GB, 30 GB of RAM, a day
~/data/ninespecies/.venv/bin/python ~/data/ninespecies/scripts/page_numbers.py --check
```

[`run_all.sh`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/run_all.sh)
lists the steps in order: list the three MassIVE deposits, fetch the HTTP
sources ([`sources.py`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/sources.py)
names every one), extract one table per source file, key every version on
*(species, raw file, scan)*, run the comparisons, and finally
[`page_numbers.py`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/page_numbers.py),
which computes every number on this page. Its `--check` compares the result
with the committed
[`page_numbers.json`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/page_numbers.json),
which is what this page prints. The charts read
[`site_data.json`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/site_data.json),
written by
[`export_site_data.py`](https://github.com/BioGeek/awesome_de_novo_peptide_sequencing/blob/main/analysis/nine_species/export_site_data.py)
in the same run.
